messages:
carlos_support: Hey team — Sentinel (customer) opened a ticket: after we onboarded Orpheus-v2 to their Dedicated pool last night they're seeing p99 CPU/GPU latency spikes for long-context generation (>24k tokens). Observed p95 is fine, p99 up ~3x baseline. Ticket: #SENT-842. Posting logs and repro below.

maya_eng_ml: Thanks Carlos. Can you dump a minimal repro (curl or SDK) and the request metadata (max_tokens, sampling, model_variant)? Also which tokenizer profile did we pick for Orpheus-v2? :eyes:

carlos_support: Copying the snippet the customer used: 

```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  -d '{"model":"orpheus-v2","input":"<~24k tokens prompt>","max_tokens":4096,"stream":false}'
```

They used default tokenizer profile "orpheus-bpe-v3" and no special quantization. Config in Dedicated: autoscale off, capacity 4xA100, route -> us-west2.

liam_eng_runtime: Noted. Can you paste the server-side tail logs for a p99 request? Also whether KV cache hits look normal?

carlos_support: Paste of one p99 request trace (stripped): 

```
[2026-09-12T03:14:22Z] req_id=sn-3f8 token_len=24680 model=orpheus-v2 variant=fp16 route=us-west2 dedicated_pool=sentinel-4xA100
[2026-09-12T03:14:22Z] batch_id=1789 batch_size=1 kv_cache_hit=false kv_entries=0
[2026-09-12T03:14:24Z] kernel_select=attention_sparse fallback=softmax_longseq path=slow
[2026-09-12T03:14:25Z] generation_start
[2026-09-12T03:14:40Z] generation_end latency=18.2s p99_expected~6s
[2026-09-12T03:14:40Z] resp_sent status=200 tokens_out=4096
```

carlos_support: Customer also tried smaller chunking (split prompt into two requests) and saw similar tail latency.

maya_eng_ml: Looks like kernel selection chose a slow long-sequence path (attention_sparse fallback) and KV cache shows misses. Two hypotheses: 1) tokenizer behavior changed for certain unicode sequences causing larger token counts and shifting kernel selection thresholds, 2) KV cache keying/serialization mismatch for this variant in Dedicated.

lia m_eng_runtime: (typo in previous) liam_eng_runtime: I can reproduce locally with a synthetic 24k token prompt — I see the same kernel fallback for orpheus-bpe-v3 when sequence length crosses 20k. We recently shipped a micro-optimization in tokenizer normalization that changes some merge boundaries; it can increase token counts by 5-7% for emoji-heavy inputs. That could push sequences into the slow attention branch.

tia_prod: Customer says this started immediately after our onboarding of orpheus-v2 last night. Can we validate if the onboarding used the latest tokenizer commit? If yes, rollback as mitigation?

sophie_oncall: I can roll back tokenizer profile on their Dedicated pool to the previous stable build (orpheus-bpe-v2) as a quick mitigation — will need a redeploy window (5m) and safe fallback check. Any objections?

liam_eng_runtime: No objection. Also propose a runtime tweak: temporarily lower the longseq kernel threshold to avoid fallback thrashing (increase threshold so sequences up to 30k use optimized path) — but that might increase memory. For Dedicated we can bump KV cache allocation and TTL to reduce misses.

maya_eng_ml: Longer term: we should add an onboarding check that compares token_count distributions for a representative prompt set and flags >3% token inflation vs baseline. Also add an automated canary where we run p95/p99 generation tests with 8 long-context prompts.

carlos_support: Customer accepted the rollback plan. Sophie — please proceed when ready and post the deploy-bot confirmation. I'll tell Sentinel to expect a 5 min maintenance window.

deployment-bot: started redeploy of tokenizer-profile "orpheus-bpe-v2" to pool sentinel-4xA100 at 2026-09-12T04:03:12Z (id: dep-9921)

deployment-bot: completed redeploy dep-9921 at 2026-09-12T04:07:31Z — health checks OK ; rolling restart of workers completed.

carlos_support: Rolled back, customer reports initial improvement: p99 down from ~18s to ~6.5s on a couple test requests. They're continuing to test production traffic.

maya_eng_ml: Great. Action items: 1) eng-ml to run tokenizer diff and add token-count gating to onboarding (owner: maya) 2) eng-runtime to add KV cache and kernel-threshold telemetry per model-variant (owner: liam) 3) support to monitor Sentinel for 24h and confirm no regressions (owner: carlos).

liam_eng_runtime: I'll also add a quick guard in the serving layer to log when kernel fallback is triggered along with token_count so we can correlate in future.

carlos_support: Thanks everyone. I'll update ticket #SENT-842 and mark as high-priority-watching for 24h. If customer re-sees tail spikes I'll reopen escalation. :thumbsup:
